text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Russia will repay a six million dollar tranche of its debt to Slovakia with the delivery of equipment for the construction of oil storage tanks for Transpetrol a.s., a state-run company operating the transfer of Russian oil to western Europe through Slovakia.
- Trade unions, the government and the employers association are expected to discuss the so-called 13th salary for civil service employees.

- Czech Airlines (CSA), one of the few airlines operating regular direct routes to and from the Slovak capital Bratislava, has threatened to cancel its flights to Slovakia after Bratislava airport authorities said they would not extend a licence for CSA's Slovak subsidiary responsible for passenger service.
- The Slovak textile and clothing industry last year recorded a foreign trade surplus of 1.7 billion crowns.

PRAVDA - The paper quotes National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) sources as saying NBS governor Vladimir Masar last Monday sent a letter to Czech central bank governor Jozef Tosovsky demanding return of the Slovak part of the former Czechoslovak gold reserves.
PRACA - Slovakia has officially demanded explanation of a U.S. foreign ministry statement that "Slovakia's democratic and free market reforms were proceding slower than in the Czech republic."

SME - The Slovak state-owned gas monopoly SPP and the Russian gas supplier Gazprom are expected to sign an agreemnent on the creation of a joint-venture to manage gas transport to western Europe during Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin's visit to Bratislava on April 28 and 29.
- The opposition Democratic Party (DS) said the planned gas joint-venture will be disadvantageous for Slovakia due to multi-billion debts of the Russian firm.
- Analysts said the Slovak government should wait with signing the SPP-Gazprom deal until the Russian government decides on Gazprom's future structure.
NARODNA OBRODA - Czech Railways have rejected Slovakia's claims to repay an estimated 126 million crowns damages caused by a recent strike of Czech railway workers.
